correctness.rationale: The coordinatewise maximization is exhaustive for every \(\lambda>0\) and every finite-dimensional \(y\). It gives \(h_\lambda^*(y)=\|S(y)\|_2^2/(2\lambda)\). Comparing the two signs in the prox-value expansion yields the exact defect \(\|C(y)\|_2^2/\lambda\); the one-sided derivative drop at \(1\) proves the printed expression is nonconvex. The corrected dual displays follow by direct substitution into the source’s Lemma 1. Exact-rational replay returned VERIFY_OK. The proof does not infer an infinite statement from finite tests.

value.rationale: The discrepancy is in explicit examples meant to instantiate a smooth convex dual algorithm. Literal use of the printed formula produces a nonconvex objective and therefore breaks the intended structural interpretation. The correction restores convexity and \(1/\lambda\)-smoothness and gives materially simpler squared-soft-threshold objectives for both examples. This is implementation-relevant and not an arbitrary algebraic slice, while the scope is kept narrow enough not to overstate consequences for the general theory.
